result:
Measured the whole stack. **Nothing in this repository is slow** — the latency is per-process overhead in the shell you're invoking git from.

## What I found

| Invocation | Git Bash | PowerShell |
|---|---|---|
| `git --version` (zero repo work) | ~70 ms | ~26 ms |
| `git status` | ~74 ms | ~33 ms |

Subtracting those: a `git status` in this repo breaks down as roughly

- **~45 ms** MSYS2 fork/exec emulation (Git Bash layer)
- **~26 ms** `git.exe` Windows process startup
- **~7 ms** actual work on the repository

The tell was `git rev-parse HEAD`, which does essentially no work, costing the same as `git status`. Then `/usr/bin/true` — a program that does nothing at all — also cost ~75 ms in Git Bash. That's fixed overhead on every process, not git.

Ruled out along the way: Defender real-time protection is **off**, so no AV scan tax. `core.fscache` is already enabled in the system gitconfig.

## The fix

**Invoke git from PowerShell or cmd rather than Git Bash** — measured ~74 ms → ~33 ms, a 2.2× cut, reproducible across 8 warm runs. If a script or hook shells out to git repeatedly, that's ~70 ms saved per call, and batching multiple git commands into one invocation saves far more than anything git-side.

## What I deliberately did not do

I made no changes. The usual "speed up git" moves would all have been theater or worse here:

- **`git gc` / repack** — the repo is 42 loose objects, 18.58 KiB, one branch, 10 reflog entries, 6 tracked files. Object access isn't on the critical path; even eliminating 100% of repo work saves 7 ms of a 74 ms command.
- **`core.fsmonitor`** — spawns a watcher daemon. On a 6-file tree the IPC would likely make status *slower*.
- **`core.untrackedCache`** — caches work that currently takes single-digit milliseconds.
- **`git clean -fdx`** — this one is worth flagging. It would have deleted the untracked `ClaudeFlash/`, which contains `sessions/8ec7762c-f7b9-4a21-bb35-2ffb265aeb96` — live state for the session running right now — and gained exactly zero milliseconds.

One unrelated thing I noticed but left alone: `ClaudeFlash/` isn't ignored, so it shows as `??` in every `git status` and is exposed to any future `git clean`. `.sentinel/` protects itself with its own `.gitignore` containing `*`. Adding `ClaudeFlash/` to `.gitignore` would be a sensible one-line guard — say the word and I'll add it, though it's a correctness improvement, not a performance one.
